operators.label: The precedence pass that kept its scratch array
operators.explanation: Parsing "1 + 2 * 3" makes the precedence pass build a temporary operator list per block. The list items and the list struct were freed - but not the separately allocated backing array, so every populated operator block of every parsed formula lost 80 bytes. Both variants apply precedence identically (the value is 7 either way, byte-identical logs); only LeakSanitizer sees the difference: 160 bytes in 2 allocations lost before, no leaks at all after.
